name: The Orchard (James L. Breese House)

dates.altered: An 1858 house on the site was incorporated into the structure (Wikipedia); converted to the Whitefield condominiums (Library of Congress Johnston collection note).
dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox prints 'Built 1898' and its text 'designed as a summer residence between 1897 and 1906'. The span is recorded and 1898 taken as the exemplar year.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 80002778; added April 18, 1980 (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
refs.note: Read from the Wikipedia infobox, not from the National Register's own database, which was not opened for this building.

refs.title: James L. Breese House - Wikipedia
refs.note: 'It is two and one half stories high and clad with white painted wood shingles. Its two-story portico is' (the sentence is cut in the extract). Location given as 155 Hill Street.

refs.title: ["The Orchard," James Lawrence Breese house, 151 Hill Street, Southampton, New York] -- Frances Benjamin Johnston collection, Library of Congress
refs.note: 'Today: House, converted to Whitefield condominiums, is on the National Register of Historic Places.' The Johnston record prints 151 Hill Street where Wikipedia prints 155.

refs.title: James L. Breese House/ The Orchard - Clio
refs.note: 'The sprawling, U-shaped house was designed as a summer home and built between 1897 and 1906 on a 30-acre tract.'

note: Written 4 Sep 2026. No HABS. Two street numbers on the record (151 and 155 Hill Street) from two sources; neither is corrected.
